reviews.reason: The submitted English conceals a substantive textual problem. The Greek prints a height comparison, but p.61 note 13 distinguishes Ethiopic readings and editorial reconstruction. The bracketed [ኵሎሙ፡] cannot simply become an unquestioned 'all' in 'surpassed them all': Ethiopic apparatus note 49 explicitly explains its bracketing. The height expression and following verb also need exact glyph-level reconciliation; the candidate cannot be approved merely because its English is intelligible.
reviews.footnote_changes: Remove the claim that this is merely an uncertain OCR reading. Charles discusses differing readings and reconstruction on p.61, Greek note 13 and Ethiopic notes 47–49. The bracketed “all” is editorially questioned. “Rose above them” follows the Greek comparison and must be identified as such if adopted.' Keep any throne-seat explanation at 'seat of a throne', not after the opening location clause. Do not present Charles’s reports of manuscript readings as independently checked manuscripts.

reviews.reason: The English omits most of the numbered unit. XXIV.4 begins on p.60 and continues at the top of p.62 through the palm-cluster comparison, before the printed numeral 5. reviews.reason: This is a separate numbered unit on p.62, not part of Michael’s reply. The English should preserve the separate descriptions of leaves and fruit rather than merge them into one past-tense predicate. More importantly, the apparatus directly addresses both difficult expressions: note 9 contrasts the appearance wording with Greek fragrance wording, and note 10 calls the printed fruit expression corrupt for flowers. Those are editorial judgments reported by Charles, not independently verified manuscript findings.

reviews.reason: Correct the corrupted ፩እምፄ to ፩እምነ. Michael is designated one of the holy and honored/glorious angels; the unit does not explicitly call him an archangel.
